info.title: Remote participant API
info.summary: What a black-box solver serves so a coordinator can plan its device(s) with the rest of the house.
info.description: A participant is one device, or a group of devices its own solver plans together (a vendor's EV charger optimiser, EMHASS in another container, a heat pump's controller). The coordinator never sees its model: it asks what-if questions - 'your cheapest plan if your energy cost these prices' - and, once it has chosen, commits one plan. Queries are side-effect free; only a commit changes what the device does. The bodies are JSON Schemas beside this file: device-query.v1.json and device-answer.v1.json. The server URL is the API's base, below which /v1/describe and the rest live (an EMHASS serving its devices: http://host:5000/participant). EMHASS implements both sides: emhass.coordinator.remote.RemoteParticipant (the coordinator's) and ParticipantService (the solver's, served at /participant/v1/). Status: draft. Versioning: the major version is in every path (/v1/) and body (version: 1). Within a major version the API only grows - new optional fields, new values, new routes - and its minor version (info.version) says how far. A reader ignores fields it does not know, and treats a value it does not know as conservatively as it can (a commit state it does not know: not known). Response schemas are open to new fields for that reason; request schemas are closed, so a participant refuses what it cannot honour. What a participant serves beyond the first draft it lists in its description's features (commit_status: the commit record, idempotent commits and GET /v1/commit/{commit_id}); a coordinator sends a new optional field, or calls a new route, only to a participant that lists the feature. A change that would break a reader is a new major version, served beside this one (/v2/).

servers.description: the participant, on the local network

get.summary: What this participant is and which questions it answers.

post.summary: A feasible plan with no price given: what it would do uncoordinated (its thermostat, its plan at the import tariff).
Answer one what-if question. MUST NOT change what the device does or will do.
post.description: price_response is the question Dantzig-Wolfe asks - typically a few dozen per plan, so answer in well under a second; its price_draw and price_supply may differ (what drawing costs and supplying is worth at the participant's connection). best_response carries the rest of the house's load (residual_kw): it is sent only to a participant that lists it among its kinds, as it reveals the household's behaviour. proximal is ADMM's step. A horizon the participant cannot plan (another slot length) is 409. A participant that cannot solve answers with a plan it can run and status 'fallback' (the coordinator then proves no bound from it), never with an error.

post.summary: Optional, for a modulating participant: its own plan for a weighted mix of plans it answered.

200.description: The mixed plan, as it would run it.

post.summary: The plan the coordinator chose: run it. The only call with an effect.
post.description: Names the answer chosen by its Query-Id (query_id), which is the commit's id, and repeats its plan; the participant runs that answer as it gave it, and refuses (409) a query_id it did not answer on this horizon or a plan_kw that is not that answer's. It answers at once (202, state running) and runs the plan after; its outcome is then at GET /v1/commit/{commit_id}. A commit sent again with an id it has is never run twice: it answers that commit's record (200 once final, 202 while running), and 409 if the plan_kw differs. So a coordinator whose commit got no answer asks for its outcome, and sends it again only if the participant never had it (404).

200.description: A commit it already had, and how it ended (sent again), or one it refused at once (it runs no plans).

202.description: Taken: it runs now (state running). Ask GET /v1/commit/{commit_id} for its outcome.

429.description: Busy (its own optimization runs): refused, nothing was run. It may be sent again.

get.summary: What became of a commit: running, accepted, refused or partial.
get.description: Records are kept at least 48 hours, and across a restart; a commit still running when the participant stopped is read back as partial.

QueryId.name: Query-Id
QueryId.description: The coordinator's id for this answer, so a later commit can name the plan it chose.

mutualTLS.description: Preferred on a local network: both ends present certificates (a Matter fabric or EEBus SHIP pairing can issue them).

bearer.description: A token the user pairs once, for participants that cannot do mutual TLS.

start.description: The first slot planned. Required: a participant answers from a model built for given slots (its state of charge, its forecasts).

key.description: Its name in the coordinator (a device, or devices joined by '+').

max_power_kw.description: The most it can draw or supply in one slot.

modulating.description: A weighted mix of its plans runs as it is (and /v1/blend may be called).

onoff.description: Its plans are on/off schedules: fix it to one plan before re-pricing the others.

kinds.description: The query kinds it answers; price_response is required for Dantzig-Wolfe. Listing best_response agrees to be sent the rest of the house's load.

state_unit.description: The unit of its trajectory (kWh stored, degC, ...).

features.description: What it serves beyond the first draft of this version. commit_status: the commit record, idempotent commits and GET /v1/commit/{commit_id}. A coordinator ignores features it does not know.

active_commit.description: Its latest commit and how it ended, so each run starts from what it actually did.

weights.description: Query-Id -> weight; the weights sum to 1.

plan_kw.description: kW per slot, positive when drawn: the plan to run.

query_id.description: The query it answered, if it is one plan; absent for a blend.

local_price.description: Optional: the price its energy was coordinated at (currency/kWh per slot), for its own fast re-planning.

state.description: running: it publishes now. accepted: it runs the plan. refused: nothing was published. partial: publishing failed part way, so some of the plan may run (a coordinator keeps its part in the plan).

accepted.description: true if accepted, false if refused, null otherwise.

terms.description: Reserved: what following the plan is worth to each side. Null in this version.

signatures.description: Reserved: each side's signature on this record. Empty in this version.
